claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be equilibrated as a BCC phase at high temperature.
An Al content of about 7 at.% is sufficient to change the thermodynamic stability of BCC in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
At high temperature, the free energy of BCC Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is lower than that of competing FCC or intermetallic states.
Higher Al content generally favors BCC formation in Al-containing complex concentrated alloys.
The target alloy's 7 at.% Al enthalpically stabilizes BCC relative to competing phases at high temperature.
Kinetic barriers can delay phase transformations and affect phase selection in multicomponent alloys.
Sluggish multicomponent diffusion is the relevant kinetic barrier delaying transformation in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Local Al-Ni chemical ordering or short-range clustering modulates the local free-energy landscape.
Local Al-Ni ordering acts together with diffusion kinetics to delay or promote phase transformation.
A rapid quench from the high-temperature regime should retain a predominantly BCC structure.
Slow cooling or prolonged annealing below about 700 degrees Celsius should decrease the BCC fraction and produce FCC or intermetallic phases.
Sigma phase is a possible product of slow cooling or prolonged annealing of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The extent of transformation should correlate with annealing time and cooling rate.
Annealing at approximately 1100 degrees Celsius will ensure a uniform BCC starting state in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The proposed mechanism applies near Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 and where thermodynamic free-energy differences are significant above approximately 1000 degrees Celsius.
Current thermodynamic databases can give unreliable phase-stability predictions for multicomponent alloys because of incomplete assessments and missing interaction descriptions.
Exact transformation temperatures, phase fractions, free-energy differences, and kinetic barriers for the target alloy remain uncertain.
Failure of slow cooling or extended annealing to reduce BCC or create a cooling-rate or time dependence would falsify the proposed thermodynamic-kinetic mechanism.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the hypothesis applies where free-energy differences are significant above approximately 1000 degrees Celsius, while the proposed discriminating transformation and falsification test are centered at or below approximately 700 degrees Celsius. The thermal range over which the hypothesis is claimed to apply is therefore inconsistent with the principal test regime.
